assessor: RTS implementation preflight — False-Green Test Adequacy Gate v1
rationale: Repository-local testing layer over completed K1. K2 does not alter K1 production behavior, call providers, execute external probes, mutate profiles, decide semantic truth, or grant runtime authority. It evaluates test adequacy using explicit synthetic/held-out fixtures and bounded temporary mutations, with fail-closed treatment of invalid mutants and mandatory control mutants.
existing_assumptions: K1 targeted tests are deterministic and repository-local.
K2 may copy K1 into a temporary directory but must not mutate the checked-out production file in-place.
A mutation that cannot import/compile is invalid, not a behavioral kill.
No single test lane is sufficient to prove adequacy.

data_migration.notes: No K1/K0 or prior FREEZER history is mutated in place.

external_interfaces: synthetic known-bad and held-out fixture definitions
bounded mutation manifest and result report
approval_changes: none; K2 emits only test-adequacy evidence
regression_tests: K2 known-bad injection baseline + destructive DA
critical mutation kill tests with validity precheck
hidden_dependencies: critical mutation must load successfully before a failing behavioral test counts as KILLED
invalid mutant is never counted in the numerator
equivalent/no-op control must survive targeted tests
known-bad expected behavior is defined independently of the implementation under test
held-out fixtures are not reused to tune K1 escape-route rules
meaning-preserving transformations preserve the required disposition/invariant
meaning-changing transformations have an explicit expected behavioral change
all lanes preserve cardinality and audit failures
ADEQUATE requires every mandatory lane to pass
a surviving critical mutant forces HOLD even if overall kill percentage is high
rollback_boundary: Drop the K2 branch or revert test_adequacy_gate, K2 tests/workflow, and FRZ-000023 append-only records; completed K1 and A-K0 remain untouched.
completion_conditions: every critical valid mutant is killed by K1 targeted behavioral tests
no critical mutant is counted as killed solely because of syntax/import/setup failure
known-bad corpus detects every seeded safety violation
held-out corpus passes explicit expectations without tuning K1
metamorphic meaning-changing cases trigger explicit expected differences
one lane cannot mask failure in another lane
K2 report retains every mutant/case result without silent truncation
K1 production source hash is unchanged by K2 execution
A-K2 regressions and FREEZER verify pass
risks: Mutation operators are source-shape sensitive and may require explicit revalidation after K1 changes.
Held-out synthetic cases do not prove coverage of every future provider wording.
Passing K2 increases confidence but never proves absence of unknown bugs.
